answer: Each key may register exactly one survey claim — either a knoll or a hollow coordinate — and must keep a 2 GiB, key-bound work archive whose Merkle root is published every hour as an execution mirror. Validators request an unpredictable 4 KiB leaf; the agent must return it with a path that matches the root. Encoding prevents sharing or fast regeneration, so ten aliases need ten claims and 20 GiB held continuously. Five established peers attest only after a passed leaf check; a reused coordinate or a missed leaf drops the claim for the epoch.
